name: Thost-Unna Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Thost-Unna Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Diffuse, symmetric hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles
Histopathological evidence of non-epidermolytic hyperkeratosis without epidermal blistering
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Absence of epidermolytic changes differentiating from epidermolytic PPK
Onset of symptoms in early childhood

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of diffuse symmetric palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with histopathological confirmation of non-epidermolytic hyperkeratosis and a compatible family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but is not always diagnostic; differentiation from other PPK types is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse symmetric hyperkeratosis of palms and soles
pathognomonic.notes: Thickened, yellowish plaques covering entire palmoplantar surfaces
searchTerms: symmetrical thickened skin on palms and soles
evenly distributed palm and sole calluses
diffuse hyperkeratosis on hands and feet

pathognomonic.notes: Absence of epidermolysis on skin biopsy
Family history of similar palmoplantar keratoderma

searchTerms: fissured skin on hands and feet
splitting skin on palms and soles
slight skin inflammation beneath rough patches

common.symptomName: Onset in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: signs appearing in babies or young kids

common.symptomName: Absence of blistering or epidermal fragility
searchTerms: absence of skin peeling or blisters
excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet

occasional.notes: Due to fissuring and skin barrier disruption
searchTerms: skin infections from bacteria or fungi

occasional.notes: Thickened or brittle nails occasionally observed

rare.notes: Rare involvement of dorsal hands or feet
searchTerms: psoriasis-like plaques outside hands and feet
scaly red patches beyond palmoplantar regions

rare.notes: Severe cases may limit walking or manual tasks

searchTerms: swelling of limbs due to lymph fluid

genetic: Mutations in keratin genes KRT1 or KRT9 associated with disease
other: Clinical examination revealing diffuse palmoplantar thickening

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in KRT1 or KRT10 genes
Focal hyperkeratosis localized to pressure points

redFlags: Rapid progression of hyperkeratosis beyond palms and soles
Development of painful fissures with secondary infection
Signs of systemic involvement or blistering
